title: Respect upower's "should be ignored" tag when determining whether or not to notify about low battery
line: Mice and keyboards that only report a rough battery level now warn when that level turns low, instead of whenever UPower's guessed percentage looks low.
explanation: Devices such as Logitech HID++ mice and keyboards only report a coarse battery level (Normal, Low, …), and UPower turns it into an approximate percentage it marks "should be ignored". Solid had no battery level, so powerdevil compared that approximate percentage with the peripheral low-battery threshold: it alerted when a device reporting Normal appeared with e.g. 10%, and missed a Normal→Low change whose rough percentage stayed above the threshold. Solid now exposes Battery::batteryLevel() (None, Unknown, Critical, Low, Normal, High, Full) with a batteryLevelChanged signal, read from UPower's BatteryLevel. Powerdevil ignores the percentage of such devices and alerts once when their level becomes Low or Critical (on connect, at login, or on a level change), keeping the last known level while the device is asleep (Unknown) so waking it doesn't alert again; the title then leaves out the meaningless percentage.

commits.message:
battery: Add batteryLevel

Many wireless mice and keyboards only report a coarse level like Normal
or Low, and the percentage UPower derives from it is an approximation.
Add the level and a change signal so users can rely on it instead.

CCBUG: 457893

daemon: Use the battery level for peripherals that report one

Devices like Logitech mice only report a coarse level, and the rough
percentage UPower derives from it kept triggering low battery alerts.
For such devices, alert when the level becomes low or critical instead.

BUG: 457893

media.caption: Master: a Logitech M705 reporting level Normal with an approximate 10% connects and gets "Mouse Battery Low (10% Remaining)"
With the fix, the same device connects with no popup
Master: the mouse's level goes Normal → Low; the popup shows UPower's made-up 10%
With the fix, the level change gives one "Mouse Battery Low" popup without a fake percentage
Master with the peripheral threshold at 5%: the level goes Normal → Low (approximate 10%) and nothing is shown
With the fix, the same Normal → Low change warns, because the device's own level is used

review.text: Exposing Solid::Battery::batteryLevel() across Solid backends and consuming it in PowerDevil is the right architectural layer and cleanly eliminates false alerts from UPower's approximate percentages, with strong before/after evidence. However, PowerDevil unconditionally calls the new Solid 6.33 API while leaving KF6_MIN_VERSION at 6.30, which will break builds against KF 6.30–6.32 unless guarded or bumped. In addition, Core::emitPeripheralBatteryNotification() still rejects notifications when b->chargePercent() <= 0 even on the coarse-level path (percent < 0), contradicting ignoring UPower's percentage.
changes: In powerdevil, either guard the new Solid::Battery::batteryLevel API with `#if SOLID_VERSION >= QT_VERSION_CHECK(6, 33, 0)` (including `<solid_version.h>`) or bump `KF6_MIN_VERSION` to 6.33.0 once Plasma requires it, so builds against KF 6.30–6.32 do not fail.

In `Core::emitPeripheralBatteryNotification()`, restrict the `b->chargePercent() <= 0` guard to the percentage-based path (`percent >= 0`) so coarse-level notifications truly ignore UPower's approximate percentage (and won't be suppressed if a Critical/Low device reports 0%).
In solid, add an autotest covering the new public `Solid::Battery::batteryLevel()` API (e.g. via the fakehw backend).

reviews.text: The diagnosis is right: Logitech-style peripherals report a coarse UPower BatteryLevel and the percentage powerdevil threshold-compared is UPower's '(should be ignored)' approximation. Exposing Solid::Battery::batteryLevel() with a change signal and having powerdevil alert once on the Normal->Low/Critical transition (keeping the last level through Unknown/sleep, dropping the fake percentage from the title) is a sound design, and the dbusmock evidence covers connect, transition, threshold, sleep/wake and recharge cases. The refactor of the notification body into emitPeripheralBatteryNotification is behavior-preserving for percentage devices. However, powerdevil now calls Solid API marked \since 6.33 while its KF6_MIN_VERSION stays 6.30, so it no longer builds against its own declared minimum.
changes: Bump powerdevil's KF6_MIN_VERSION to the Frameworks release that ships Solid::Battery::batteryLevel() in the same MR (or guard the new code with a SOLID_VERSION check), and state the dependency on the solid MR in the description
